entry.title: The Commission's transition timeline for legacy devices and for Regulation devices placed on the market before mandatory use (an undated one-page…
entry.summary: The Commission's transition timeline for legacy devices and for Regulation devices placed on the market before mandatory use (an undated one-page Commission document linked from the EUDAMED overview page) gives 28 November 2026 as the "Deadline to register the device in the UDI/Dev module", after the notice published in the Official Journal on 27 November 2025, mandatory use of the UDI/Dev module from 28 May 2026 and a 6-month transition period. Decision (EU) 2025/2371 itself states no calendar date. 28 November 2026 is a Saturday, so ClinicOps plans to finish by Friday 27 November 2026.
entry.content:
The Commission's transition timeline for legacy devices and for Regulation devices placed on the market before mandatory use (an undated one-page Commission document linked from the EUDAMED overview page) gives 28 November 2026 as the "Deadline to register the device in the UDI/Dev module", after the notice published in the Official Journal on 27 November 2025, mandatory use of the UDI/Dev module from 28 May 2026 and a 6-month transition period. Decision (EU) 2025/2371 itself states no calendar date. 28 November 2026 is a Saturday, so ClinicOps plans to finish by Friday 27 November 2026.

Not established or limited:

  • The Commission timeline is a one-page document with no document date, no version and no legal citation, and the overview page that links it prints no November 2026 date; the date is as the Commission document labels it, read on 16 November 2026. Decision (EU) 2025/2371 states no calendar date (read on EUR-Lex through a text-extraction tool; a second look at the Official Journal PDF is advisable before the date is cited in a client deliverable).
  • Friday 27 November 2026 is a ClinicOps planning date, not a regulatory date: 28 November 2026 is a Saturday, and calendar-month counting from the 27 November 2025 publication can give 27 November 2026. ClinicOps has not established which count controls, and the earlier commentary that gave 27 November as the date is not used as a source.
  • Article 123(3)(e) MDR as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1860 refers to "no later than 12 months from the date of publication of the notice referred to in Article 34(3)" for the entry of Article 29 information for the devices listed in (e)(i) and (ii); counted from 27 November 2025 that points to 27 November 2026. This is ClinicOps' reading of the consolidated text and has not had a legal read; whether the Commission timeline's 28 November 2026 and Article 123(3)(e) describe the same obligation is not established. The Commission's undated Q&A cites Article 123(3)(d), but the consolidated text places the 12-month rule in (e) and the 6-month application rule in (d).
  • Rewritten 16 November 2026 to reconcile this claim with CO-CLM-0020 (shared fact_key and value). After 28 November 2026 the wording must move to the past tense.
  • Whether a specific device qualifies as a legacy device is a manufacturer determination.

entry.title: Under Article 22 MDR, a person who places a system or procedure pack on the market under Article 22(1) or (3) is not thereby the manufacturer of the…
entry.summary: Under Article 22 MDR, a person who places a system or procedure pack on the market under Article 22(1) or (3) is not thereby the manufacturer of the constituent devices, whereas under Article 22(4) a combination outside 22(1) and (3) is treated as a device in its own right and that person assumes the obligations of a manufacturer; Article 32 places the SS(C)P duty on the manufacturer, so on ClinicOps' reading no SS(C)P duty arises for a pack registered under Article 22(1) or (3).
entry.content:
Under Article 22 MDR, a person who places a system or procedure pack on the market under Article 22(1) or (3) is not thereby the manufacturer of the constituent devices, whereas under Article 22(4) a combination outside 22(1) and (3) is treated as a device in its own right and that person assumes the obligations of a manufacturer; Article 32 places the SS(C)P duty on the manufacturer, so on ClinicOps' reading no SS(C)P duty arises for a pack registered under Article 22(1) or (3).

Not established or limited:

  • The Article 22 and Article 32 text is primary; the conclusion that no SS(C)P duty arises for the pack is ClinicOps reasoning, not a stated Commission or MDCG position.
  • Constituent devices keep their own manufacturers' obligations, including any Article 32 duty.
  • Re-read on 16 November 2026 (EUR-Lex consolidated text of 10 January 2025, text-extraction tool). Article 22(4) is confirmed as read; the extraction of Article 22(1) did not show an express statement that the person is not the manufacturer of the constituent devices, which stays ClinicOps reading, as labelled above.

entry.title: The EUDAMED system/procedure-pack registration records the highest risk class among the devices that form part of the pack, so a class III value on a…
entry.summary: The EUDAMED system/procedure-pack registration records the highest risk class among the devices that form part of the pack, so a class III value on a PR-role record is inherited from a constituent device rather than being an ordinary classification of the pack itself; separately, MDCG 2019-9 rev.1 describes an SS(C)P document-control model in which an updated revision can exist while notified-body validation timing is in process, so a published revision may legitimately be published between validation cycles.
entry.content:
The EUDAMED system/procedure-pack registration records the highest risk class among the devices that form part of the pack, so a class III value on a PR-role record is inherited from a constituent device rather than being an ordinary classification of the pack itself; separately, MDCG 2019-9 rev.1 describes an SS(C)P document-control model in which an updated revision can exist while notified-body validation timing is in process, so a published revision may legitimately be published between validation cycles.

Not established or limited:

  • Sourced from the Commission EUDAMED Information Centre and non-binding MDCG guidance; do not convert a document-vs-record difference into an irregularity without establishing the exact process state.
  • Do not describe a system/procedure pack as itself a class III device on the strength of the inherited field.
  • Re-read on 16 November 2026: the EUDAMED help page (v2.27.0, 24 July 2026) says the class 'must be the highest risk class of devices that are part of the system or procedure pack'. MDCG 2019-9 rev.1 (March 2022) says the revision history should state whether a revision was validated by the notified body and that it should be transparent to the public whether the SS(C)P has been validated yet; it does not expressly say that a revision may be published between validations, so that clause is an inference from those two statements.

entry.title: Commission Decision (EU) 2025/2371 of 26 November 2025, published in the Official Journal on 27 November 2025, confirms four EUDAMED systems as…
entry.summary: Commission Decision (EU) 2025/2371 of 26 November 2025, published in the Official Journal on 27 November 2025, confirms four EUDAMED systems as functional: actor registration, UDI database and device registration, notified bodies and certificates, and market surveillance. It enters into force on the day of its publication and states no calendar date for mandatory use. The Commission's EUDAMED overview page states that this publication triggered a transition period of 6 months and that, as of 28 May 2026, these four modules became mandatory to use. For legacy devices the Commission's transition timeline gives 28 November 2026 as the deadline to register the device in the UDI/Dev module (see CO-CLM-0013); 28 November 2026 is a Saturday, so ClinicOps plans to finish by Friday 27 November 2026.
entry.content:
Commission Decision (EU) 2025/2371 of 26 November 2025, published in the Official Journal on 27 November 2025, confirms four EUDAMED systems as functional: actor registration, UDI database and device registration, notified bodies and certificates, and market surveillance. It enters into force on the day of its publication and states no calendar date for mandatory use. The Commission's EUDAMED overview page states that this publication triggered a transition period of 6 months and that, as of 28 May 2026, these four modules became mandatory to use. For legacy devices the Commission's transition timeline gives 28 November 2026 as the deadline to register the device in the UDI/Dev module (see CO-CLM-0013); 28 November 2026 is a Saturday, so ClinicOps plans to finish by Friday 27 November 2026.

Not established or limited:

  • Read on 16 November 2026: the Commission EUDAMED overview page, the Commission legacy-device transition timeline PDF and the Decision on EUR-Lex (Articles 1 and 2 and recitals 3 to 6) through a text-extraction tool; a second look at the Official Journal PDF is advisable before any date is cited in a client deliverable.
  • The Decision states no calendar date; 28 May 2026 and 28 November 2026 come from Commission documents that carry no document date. The Commission's undated Q&A on the gradual roll-out cites Article 123(3)(d) MDR as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1860 (the consolidated text places the 12-month rule in 123(3)(e); see CO-CLM-0013) and says registration of legacy devices must be done "within 12 months from the publication in the OJEU", but states it has not been formally endorsed by the Commission, so it is not used as a source for a date.
  • Friday 27 November 2026 is a ClinicOps planning date, not a regulatory date. Whether a specific device is in scope is a manufacturer determination.
  • The vigilance and clinical-investigation modules are not among the four modules (see CO-CLM-0050). Certificate registration has its own later date in the Commission timeline and is not covered here.
  • Rewritten 16 November 2026: the earlier text gave 27 or 28 November from commentary and described a 12-month period taken from commentary; both are replaced by what the Commission documents state.

entry.title: Under Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Articles 5 to 8, for an initial clinical trial application: validation takes 10 days (up to 25 with a request for…
entry.summary: Under Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Articles 5 to 8, for an initial clinical trial application: validation takes 10 days (up to 25 with a request for information); the Part I assessment takes 45 days from the validation date in steps of 26, 12 and 7 days, extended by up to 31 days for a request for information and by up to 50 days for expert consultation on advanced-therapy and Annex point 1 products; Part II takes 45 days, extended by up to 31 days for a request for information; the decision follows within 5 days of the later of the Part I reporting date and the end of Part II. The EMA CTIS Sponsor Handbook states 60 days without and 106 days with requests for information, and describes a pause of all timers from 22 December to 8 January.
entry.content:
Under Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Articles 5 to 8, for an initial clinical trial application: validation takes 10 days (up to 25 with a request for information); the Part I assessment takes 45 days from the validation date in steps of 26, 12 and 7 days, extended by up to 31 days for a request for information and by up to 50 days for expert consultation on advanced-therapy and Annex point 1 products; Part II takes 45 days, extended by up to 31 days for a request for information; the decision follows within 5 days of the later of the Part I reporting date and the end of Part II. The EMA CTIS Sponsor Handbook states 60 days without and 106 days with requests for information, and describes a pause of all timers from 22 December to 8 January.

Not established or limited:

  • Read from the Official Journal text (Publications Office) as consolidated to 5 December 2022; later amendments were not checked. The winter pause is an EMA/CTCG practice described in the Sponsor Handbook, not in the Regulation, and the 2026-27 dates rest on its generic wording. Weekend and holiday roll-forward follows the handbook and Regulation 1182/71 Article 3; holiday calendars belong to the Member State and are not built in. Where a request for information falls inside an assessment is not fixed by the Regulation, so the tool places it at the end of the assessment it extends. The 156-day advanced-therapy maximum is ClinicOps arithmetic, not a stated figure. Planning aid, not legal advice.

entry.title: Under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 a manufacturer outside the Union may place a device on the Union market only if it designates a sole authorised…
entry.summary: Under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 a manufacturer outside the Union may place a device on the Union market only if it designates a sole authorised representative (Article 11(1)); the designation is valid only when accepted in writing (Article 11(2)); the representative's mandate includes verifying that the declaration of conformity and technical documentation have been drawn up and meeting the Article 31 registration obligations (Article 11(3)). Before placing a device other than a custom-made device on the market, manufacturers, authorised representatives and importers submit their identification information to the electronic system (Article 31(1)); the competent authority verifies it and obtains the single registration number (Article 31(2)). Importers verify that the device is registered (Article 13(4)).

entry.summary: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1466 of 22 July 2025, published in the Official Journal on 23 July 2025, amends Implementing Regulation (EU) No 520/2012 and applies from 12 February 2026. Article 6(3) of Regulation 520/2012 as amended requires a marketing authorisation holder's pharmacovigilance subcontract to contain a clear description of the roles and responsibilities of the third parties; their obligation to exchange safety data with the holder, and the method of exchange if relevant; arrangements for inspection and auditing of the third parties; and their agreement to be audited by or on behalf of the holder and inspected by competent authorities. Article 6(4) bars onward subcontracting of assigned tasks without the holder's written consent. Article 13(1a) provides that a third party subcontracted for pharmacovigilance tasks shall be audited by or on behalf of the holder, taking into account the risk of the subcontracted activity.

entry.title: In the ClinicOps September 2026 public-source scan (extraction 8 September 2026), three convenience samples gave 69 device rows across roughly 42…
entry.summary: In the ClinicOps September 2026 public-source scan (extraction 8 September 2026), three convenience samples gave 69 device rows across roughly 42 manufacturers publishing national-language SS(C)Ps; in 22 consecutive rows of the second sample no published SS(C)P and EUDAMED record carried the same reference number and revision, the three EUDAMED-held SS(C)Ps in those rows carried a different reference from the published file, the published Basic UDI-DI matched no EUDAMED Basic UDI-DI in 6 of the 22 rows, 5 of 7 multi-language document sets were identical across languages, the systematic class III sample read 95 listing pages (4,750 UDI-DI records; 213 class III rows collapsing to 98 distinct identifiers) with linked-SS(C)P issue dates from January 2022 to August 2026 on the 17 MDR manufacturer registrations, and 103 of 103 detail lookups cross-checked clean.
entry.content:
In the ClinicOps September 2026 public-source scan (extraction 8 September 2026), three convenience samples gave 69 device rows across roughly 42 manufacturers publishing national-language SS(C)Ps; in 22 consecutive rows of the second sample no published SS(C)P and EUDAMED record carried the same reference number and revision, the three EUDAMED-held SS(C)Ps in those rows carried a different reference from the published file, the published Basic UDI-DI matched no EUDAMED Basic UDI-DI in 6 of the 22 rows, 5 of 7 multi-language document sets were identical across languages, the systematic class III sample read 95 listing pages (4,750 UDI-DI records; 213 class III rows collapsing to 98 distinct identifiers) with linked-SS(C)P issue dates from January 2022 to August 2026 on the 17 MDR manufacturer registrations, and 103 of 103 detail lookups cross-checked clean.

Not established or limited:

  • Convenience and reachable-frame samples; none of the figures are population rates and the frames saturate toward smaller firms that publish openly.
  • Content is never retrievable through the public API; 'match' means matching identifiers, never matching text.
  • Extraction was performed by language-model agents reading JSON; residual extraction error cannot be excluded.
  • Aggregates only; names no manufacturer and no device and is not a compliance statement about any company.
